newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Mercosur solders ties with associate members.
newsitem.headline: Mercosur solders ties with associate members.

text.p: The Mercosur customs union strengthened its international bargaining power Thursday by agreeing to increase political ties with associate members Chile and Bolivia.

"What is clear is that the Mercosur is made up of a political process that represents six countries," Uruguay's President Julio Sanguinetti said at the closing press conference of a meeting of Mercosur presidents in Asuncion.
Mercosur, established in 1991, groups Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. Chile reached a free trade agreement with the group last year and Bolivia entered into a similar pact recently.
The four Mercosur presidents and the heads of Chile and Bolivia who also attended the summit pointed to an increased role within the union for the associate members.

Earlier, Chile's President Eduardo Frei said: "I think that on the basis of what we are discussing here we can create, in coming months, the adequate mechanisms to maintain united action within these (external relations) and other areas."
At the same time that the group vowed to deepen its internal integration, it hoped to expand in Latin America with a view to establishing Americas-wide free trade.

More members are likely to boost the group's political weight in negotiations on establishing a Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA) to confront the United States on disagreements over what issues to prioritize in the talks.
At a meeting of trade ministers from across the Americas in Brazil in May, Mercosur frustrated the United States by leaving the issue of how to negotiate the creation of the FTAA until next year.
The leaders said they expected negotiations on free trade agreements with Peru, Ecuador, Colombia and Venezuela to be concluded this year.
They added that they hoped bilateral deals with Mexico could be concluded in 1997.
"The countries of the Southern cone (of Latin America) deserve more than anything else to assume a position of leadership in the negotiations," Frei said in his speech.
At a meeting of 34 heads of American states in Miami in 1994, it was agreed to work towards the creation of FTAA in 2005.

Argentina's President Carlos Menem pointed out that Mercosur could provide the muscle to create a link-up with the North American Free Trade Area (NAFTA) which groups the United States, Canada and Mexico.
He said that a member of his government had recently returned from Canada saying that that country was also interested in becoming a part of Mercosur.
"If we add to this the interest of the Mexicans, within a short period of time the United States is going to want to incorporate itself in Mercosur as well," he said.
"This is a signal that things are working well, that here we are working seriously, that we are credible and have the confidence of the whole world," said Menem.
While having a firm eye on FTAA, the leaders "reiterated their wish to strengthen relations with the European Union," said the presidents' joint declaration signed Thursday.
They hoped a joint summit of European Union and Mercosur leaders would take place, as recently suggested by French and German politicians visiting Latin America.
